rv.q: Even if you never thought about traveling to Norway, you'll probably want to visit the inevitably titled "Oslo," the absorbing drama by Mr. Rogers...At a very full three hours, with many international stops, this play is long and dense enough to make you wonder if you should have packed an overnight bag.
J. T. Rogers’s gripping, big-boned Oslo, which opened last night at Lincoln Center Theater, needs all the meat and muscle it can pack on its frame.
J. T. Roger's Oslo is gripping, provocative, wrenching, funny and altogether riveting.
It transforms three hours of talk about the Oslo Accords into gripping and urgent entertainment.
The performances are excellent and the spare, video-enhanced staging is seamless, accommodating swift changes in setting.
The play itself succeeds in drawing us into the minutiae of now dimly remembered diplomatic brawling.

You need some solidity, whether in the conclusion or in the lack of one, but the most you get here is a flimsy, tacked-on epilogue that details the various deaths and derailments of the characters, as though any of that is (or has been) the point.
